To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Transformer model can be quantized with minimal accuracy drop and that the Transformer model is highly parallelizable and can achieve high throughput on Intel CPUs.
we present novel quantization methods directly in TensorFlow to transform a Transformer machine language translation FP32 computational graph into an efficient INT8/VNN.

we quantize the Transformer neural machine language translation model with less than 0,5% accuracy loss using INT8/VNN1 instructions in Intel Xeon Cascade Lake processors, which delivers 1.5x improvement over best FP32 performance, and we present novel quantization methods and bin-packing techniques to maximize CPU utilization and performance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Transformer language translation model can be efficiently quantized with INT8/VNIN instructions to achieve 1.5$\times$ performance improvement on Intel CPUs.
we have quantized the Transformer model and achieved 1.5 times better inference performance on the latest Intel Xeon Cascade Lake processor with less than 0,5$\%$ loss of translation accuracy.
we quantize a large Transformer neural machine language translation model and achieve 1.5x improvement in performance over the best floating point baseline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quantizing a deep learning model can be challenging and the quantization process is highly dependent on the model structure and the hardware architecture.
quantization is a promising approach for inference performance improvement.
quantization can provide a high-performance solution to run inference on Intel CPUs.
